about: Tuxedo Winnie the Pooh is a two-row comparison: on top, Pooh slumps in a blue armchair in his usual red shirt with a bored, half-lidded look; underneath, the same Pooh has been edited into a black tuxedo and bow tie, eyes closed and eyebrows raised in smug satisfaction. The empty space to the right of each picture holds the captions. The joke is the snob upgrade: the top row names the ordinary way of saying or doing something, and the bottom row names the pretentious, fancy or technically correct version that Pooh, now a man of culture, prefers. It is perfect for pompous rewordings and over-engineered alternatives.
origin: The base art comes from Disney's Winnie the Pooh cartoons. The tuxedo edit first passed around 4chan as a reaction pic and turned into a mainstream Reddit format in 2019.
usage:
The top box is the plain, everyday version: a common name, a casual habit or a normal solution. The bottom box is the elevated version, ideally a needlessly grand rewording of the exact same thing, like the default "Burger King" vs "The Monarch of Hamburg." Both captions sit to the right of the images, so keep them to a few words each.

The best captions mean the same thing in both rows and only change in tone, which makes Pooh's smugness feel unearned. Literal translations, overly formal titles and fussy tool choices all work well.
ideas: "let me get back to you on that"
